The results above provide valuable insights into harmonic emission management for hosting capacity enhancement in the context of ultrafast charging stations.

articleTitle: Low voltage network balancing to enhance photovoltaic hosting capacity - operational environment experiment with low smart meters coverage
abstract: In Belgium, a change in regulation has led to the massive installation of solar panels, which is expected to drastically worsen voltage excursions, resulting in increased PV disconnections. This paper aims to assess the benefits of network balancing to improve the voltage map and therefore increase the network hosting capacity, in an operational environment. The network balancing method that is evaluated here has been especially developed to be used with low Smart Meter coverage. The experiment has been conducted with RESA, the electricity network operator for the Liege area. The area under consideration contains data from 4 secondary sub-stations with a total of 206 customers, with a smart meter's coverage ranging from 34% to 66% depending on the considered substation.

articleTitle: Application of distribution network automatic voltage control with fully supervised system in East China
abstract: To maintain the distribution network power system stability and power quality, the automatic voltage control system (AVC) is necessary to reduce the fluctuations caused by the growth of penetration level of renewable energy and high-power appliances randomly plug in and out. The application of AVC in a city of East China distribution network is presented in this paper. The AVC application in this city is integrated design on the State Grid Intelligent Dispatching and Command System D5000 platform[1, 7]. Its main function is to ensure that the voltage and power factors are qualified under the premise of satisfying the safe and stable operation of the power grid. And to reduce the active loss caused by unnecessary reactive power flow of the system as much as possible. AVC obtains the control model from the network analysis application and the real-time data collected from the SCADA system for online analysis and calculation. It carries out centralized monitoring, unified management and online control of the on-load voltage regulating devices and reactive power compensation equipment of each substation in the power grid. The closed-loop operation of the optimal control of reactive voltage in the whole network is achieved.

articleTitle: Enabling soft open points to support local electricity markets and increase hosting capacity of distribution networks
abstract: Active network technologies, such as voltage regulators and capacitor banks have been used for decades to introduce flexibility in electricity networks. These technologies have been mostly used to optimize the techno-economic performance of networks; however, the extent to which they can support the sustainable development of distribution systems via markets has not been investigated. In this work, we investigate the potential of the novel technology, namely, Soft Open Point (SOP), to support Local Electricity Markets (LEMs) by alleviating network constraints and increasing social welfare by accommodating otherwise infeasible transactions. Particularly, to enable SOPs to support electricity markets and increase the hosting capacity of networks, the LEM clearing problem has been integrated into the SOP scheduling. Using realistic supply and demand of renewables and flexible load applied to the IEEE 33-bus system, our studies show that in the congested network, SOP-supported LEM can accommodate 40.7% more transactions in volume, leading to the social welfare increase of 41.9%. The results demonstrate that SOP technology possesses a substantial amount of value to support LEMs and establish sustainable development of distribution systems in terms of integration of renewables and distributed flexibility, which are the keys to efficient energy transition.

articleTitle: Operation of on-load tap changer (OLTC) in MV/LV transformer by using smart meter data for voltage optimization and increasing hosting capacity in low voltage distribution grids with distributed photovoltaics (DPV)
abstract: This paper presents the results from a Norwegian pilot project on using voltage regulating distribution transformers (VRDTs) in low voltage grids with DPV together with smart meter data. The aim of the project was to minimize the networks losses by purposefully adjusting the target voltage of the VRDT and, at the same time, ensuring that the voltage at all connection points meet the national limits, despite the application of increased hosting capacity. Control strategies with fixed set-point, smart-meter based dynamic set-point and a self-learning algorithm have been compared. In addition, the use of weather data as input to the control algorithm for determining the optimal voltage has been tested. Results show that VRDTs can increase the hosting capacity of low voltage networks and be used to optimize voltage, and that it is possible to use smart meter data to enable an even more dynamic voltage regulation. Some issues were identified, that should be specifically considered when installing VRDT in networks with DPV.

articleTitle: Rapid deployment of capacity and energy management systems
abstract: An accelerated energy transition calls for an efficient development of innovative energy and grid capacity management algorithms. Field tests often play a vital role in evaluating the performance of new approaches before mass rollout, but often require extensive engineering efforts. To speed up even demanding field trials, this work presents a rapid deployment methodology and its implementation. Based on several core principles that target efficient engineering and demonstration, a rapid deployment architecture is derived. The architecture is then implemented in the AIT Rapid Deployment Platform (AIT RDP) and applied in various projects. It is demonstrated that via a combination of broadly available and mature software components as well as few custom modules that bridge needed functionality, a wide range of application scenarios can be covered with minimum efforts. Although ambitious prototypes often need to be integrated in complex environments using a multitude of different communication patterns and protocols, a large share of interface logic can be reused among installations. Hence, development efforts can be considerably reduced leaving more resources for the innovative algorithms under test.

articleTitle: Probabilistic assessment of network hosting capacity
abstract: The integration of a substantial quantity of distributed renewable energy sources (DRES) with minimum environmental impact, yet with immense uncertainty in the energy production, poses significant challenges to the distribution networks (DNs). Consequently, the evaluation and enhancement of the hosting capacity (HC) of the DNs have garnered considerable attention. This paper introduces a novel planning method for increasing the HC of a DN without necessitating expensive long-term infrastructure upgrades. A proper threshold for acceptable violations of the DN’s operating voltage limits is defined and a probabilistic method for assessing the probability of occurrence of such violations is formulated, based on Monte Carlo (MC) simulations. If the probability of violations falls below the specified threshold, approval for the integration of the examined RES is granted. This framework is a relaxation of the widely applied worst-case scenario planning methodologies for addressing uncertainties in DRES integration studies. Under this approach, the maximization of the hosting capacity is formulated as a stochastic optimization problem with chance constraints. Applying this methodology to a distribution network of Greece and comparing the outcomes with the existing methodology employed by the Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) reveals a significant increase in HC for a certain set of candidate buses for PV installation.

articleTitle: Influence of the degree of meshing on the observability and reliability of monitoring systems for power system state estimation
abstract: Power system state estimation approximates the state of the power system using a sparse metering infrastructure. For the optimal placement of measurement stations, observability and reliability requirements must be considered. In this work an optimal meter placement algorithm is used with an objective function that combines both monetary cost reduction and topological distribution, as well as the number of critical measurements and sets. In the investigation, the degree of meshing is increased or decreased by the closing of breakers and the switching off of lines, respectively. Simulation results of the CIGRE medium voltage network and the IEEE 30-bus network show that the minimum number of measurements for an observable system is not influenced by the degree of meshing. However, a higher degree of meshing has a positive effect on the reliability of the monitoring system as the number of critical measurements and sets is reduced.

articleTitle: Optimising grid planning in Paris: the challenge of long-term forecasting electricity demand on a very local scale
abstract: To achieve the COP21 Paris Agreement goals, Paris has set ambitious targets to reduce local energy consumption and reach carbon neutrality in 2050. The City has defined its own decarbonisation measures including ambitious thermal renovation volume, large electrification (for mobility and potentially for heating) and expansion of the urban heating and cooling networks. Paris has also specific challenges (density of population, lot of protected historic districts see conf. difficulties to install heat pumps). These characteristics make it difficult to strictly transpose national forecasting models to predict an accurate evolution of electricity consumption in Paris over the long term and analyse the impact on the grid. Therefore the DSO needs to develop prospective models at a local scale. The following communication focuses on the method used to set a most accurate long-term electricity demand forecast for Paris and provides some lessons learned from this work.

articleTitle: A framework for data-driven decision support for operational planning in active distribution networks
abstract: This paper describes a framework envisioned to be part of operational planning to help Distribution System Operators (DSOs) securely operate the grid. The main two components of the framework are workflows for grid situational awareness and dynamic tariffs for implicit control of demand and distributed generation. Digital Twins (DT) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are leveraged to compose a modular framework to execute specific workflows aimed at increasing the observability of the grid state and to analyse the impact of dynamic tariffs on alleviating grid violations. Data analytics and grid modelling are applied to assimilate data, detect anomalies either due to incipient grid faults or demand and generation irregularities, calculate power flows, estimate the risk of grid violations such as cable overloading, and aid the design of effective grid tariffs. In addition to presenting the concept of the AISOP project, the Digital Process Twin (DPT) framework, progress on anomaly detection and power flow forecasting is presented, and an outlook on implementation aspects is given.

articleTitle: Combined modelling of different electric vehicle fleets for estimation of grid impact and flexibility potential
abstract: The effects of the integration of electromobility on the distribution grid are mainly considered separately for individual vehicle classes. However, when dimensioning the grid connection capacity in particular for highway rest stops, a combined consideration of different vehicle fleets is necessary. Therefore, this paper presents a modelling approach for the combined consideration of charging of passenger electric cars and electric trucks on highway rest stops based on real user behaviour data. An exemplary case study for a real highway rest stop in the south of Germany shows, that the truck charging has a much larger impact on the total combined charging load even with small degrees of electrification. It also shows that even at full electrification of passenger cars and trucks, not every car parking space needs to provide an own charging point. Furthermore, the flexibility of electric truck charging can be used to flatten the charging profile by load shifting, leading to a lower required dimensioning of the grid connection. Therefore, with the presented approach, it is possible to predict the combined worst-case power demand of passenger electric cars and trucks on highway rest stops.

articleTitle: Impacts of distributed generation on travelling wave-based fault locators in medium voltage radial feeders: an analysis for different hosting capacity scenarios
abstract: The growing penetration of renewable energy in distribution networks has led utilities to make their systems more flexible and able to operate in a decentralised way. As this penetration becomes more prevalent, it is necessary to readapt fault location algorithms due to a potential paradigm shift. In this study, an analysis was made of travelling wave-based fault locators applied to medium voltage radial feeders with the presence of photovoltaic panels. The proposed approach incorporates the Wavelet transform and empirical mode decomposition to improve the precision rate of a fault locator. In addition, the behaviour of single-ended and double-ended travelling wave algorithms was verified. The simulations were executed using the PSCAD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>/EMTP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>software, where a CIGRE 14-buses medium voltage test distribution system was considered. The results showed promising precision (ranging from 0.02% to 1.8%), demonstrating that the proposed approach is not only a technological possibility, but also an accurate fault locator to ensure system’s reliability and efficiency under different hosting capacity scenarios.

articleTitle: Utilising the potential of demand side flexibility of an energy community for increasing the hosting capacity of distribution grids
abstract: The conducted study evaluates the interoperability between prosumer oriented self-consumption and grid operator oriented community level provision of grid services such as load-shifting and peak-shaving by the prosumers of an energy community. The study considers the inherent motivation of households to perform self-consumption, however when a household has opted for performing a grid service, the grid service is prioritised. The impact of performing such a community level grid service on individual household daily self-consumption and daily self-sufficiency is investigated, compared and assessed at the PCC of the energy community. The conducted study models an energy community based on an actual testing grid setup to increase the scalability of the approach. Type days are used for analysing the potential of load-shifting or peak-shaving in sunny, cloudy and passage of cloud conditions. Furthermore, varying shares of participation in the grid services provision are taken into consideration to account for the varying priorities of households in the energy community. The results show in some cases approximately 50% reduction in peak load through grid service provision with only a minor impact on the individual household degree of daily self-consumption and a comparatively significant up to a 40%pt. deviation in the individual household daily self-sufficiency.

articleTitle: Hosting capacity calculation across different voltage levels considering universal and local regulation-based technical constraints
abstract: The hosting capacity (HC) of additional distributed energy resources (DERs) integrated into the distribution grids is limited by multiple technical factors defined by international and national regulations. In this paper, a generic methodology for the HC calculation is presented considering the HC influence on other interconnected grids. The technical constraints include bounds for the voltage quality, and the loading of grid assets. Next, a specific use case based on the Spanish regulation is developed, considering various limits for the loading of grid assets, voltage quality, power capacity, and the short-circuit power ratio. For mesh grids, the unavailability of supply through N-1 analyses is also evaluated. It is evident that the HC is more realistically calculated due to the impact of interconnected grids, while the constraints of the Spanish regulation can restrict further the HC.

articleTitle: Effects of contract-based trading mechanism of power flexibility on hosting capacity of distribution systems
abstract: Incorporating new business and trading models in the process of hosting capacity (HC) analyses of distribution systems is of great importance. Accordingly, this paper presents a two-stage methodology to investigate the effects of flexibility contracts (FlexCons) on the HC assessment of distribution grids. In the first stage, the maximization of FlexCon exchanges between photovoltaic (PV) solar owners and demands is addressed. In the second stage, an optimization-based HC calculation is carried out for various cases with and without considering FlexCons. In particular, the impacts of location and number of FlexCons on the HC are studied. The results of simulations on a 33-bus radial distribution network indicate an increase in PV-HC by considering contract-based trading of power flexibility through FlexCons.

articleTitle: Quantifying the impact of day-ahead renewable forecasts on DER hosting capacity estimation
abstract: This research paper presents a novel optimization approach to estimate short-term hosting capacity of distributed energy resources (DER) within a local distribution network. It emphasizes how DER day-ahead forecasts at various nodes can significantly impact both total and nodal hosting capacities. By analysing these forecasts, the distribution system operator (DSO) can proactively adjust the hosting capacity estimation to ensure network short-term operational security under different scenarios. Our study case with Finnish urban network model confirms that nodes at the beginning of the feeder have higher nodal hosting capacity. Crucially, even 40% variations in DER forecasts for these high-capacity nodes can substantially affect the entire network's hosting capacity. This highlights the paramount importance of accurate DER forecasts, particularly for these critical points within the DSO network.

articleTitle: Predicting future low voltage loads: extension of a method for optimised energetic building retrofitting using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Increasing the energy efficiency of residential buildings is a major component of the energy transition in Germany. With the growing adoption of decentralised renewables in retrofitting efforts, there is an emergence of novel grid load scenarios characterised by enhanced uncertainty at the low voltage level. Nevertheless, for ensuring a stable grid operation, research is required to assess the implications of the energy transition. This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning framework for optimised energetic building retrofitting to simulate future low voltage load profiles. Within this framework, several categories of discrete building retrofit options are considered and an optimal policy for improving economic building efficiency is approximated. The outcomes indicate substantial efficiency improvements, with the outdoor temperature patterns of the respective building location playing a key role in determining the optimal actions. From the resulting retrofit concepts, high resolution load profiles can be generated and a prediction tool for estimating future grid scenarios can be derived.

articleTitle: Evaluation of requirements for an interoperable flexibility platform for balancing, redispatch and intraday markets
abstract: Flexibility in a power system encompasses a broad range of heterogeneous products and their applications. Managing them well is essential for enabling a successful energy transition. This is a challenging task because of the complexity of having multiple stakeholders, products, systems, scenarios, etc., in addition to different flexibility applications with varying needs and technical ecosystems. The work presented in this paper focuses on three interoperable use cases of flexibility for balancing, congestion management, and intraday markets. It refines their requirements to model key functions in a flexibility platform, with a focus on balancing energy considering network restrictions for practical implementation. The developed model is complemented with business, high-level, and primary use cases that describe various processes at the appropriate level of abstraction. It identifies major classes of stakeholders along with their needs, expectations, relationships, and technical interfaces. Its usage of a shared visual language and framework for depicting system requirements, design, and architecture proved useful in improving communication across multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders. Improved communication reduces misconceptions and misinterpretations, allowing for greater collaboration.

articleTitle: The DSO's online service for customers to enable efficient use of capacity with an electricity connection – case Helen DSO
abstract: The surge in clean energy investments poses a challenge in urban areas like Helsinki, Finland, where power demand at customer connection points is set to surpass current capacity. The transition to cleaner energy solutions is evident in Helsinki's properties, where the use of heat pump solutions, electric vehicle (EV) charging systems, and rooftop PV systems has increased. The growing power demand prompts customers to consider a significant increase in connection size. To address this, a Finnish distribution system operator (DSO) Helen Electricity Network Ltd. (Helen DSO) has developed an online service allowing customers to monitor their electrical load, assess available capacity, and make informed clean energy investments. This prevents unnecessary capacity reservations and promotes the use of existing free capacity, thereby reducing costly distribution network expansions in dense urban environments.

articleTitle: Co-simulation approach to study of dynamics phenomena for renewables integration into distribution power systems
abstract: The paper examines the relevance, requirements and expected benefits of co-simulation to study the stability and reliability of distribution networks with components based on power electronics (renewable energy sources) in transient modes of operation. The rules and principles of adjusting and working with the co-simulation tool are given, depending on the features of the network model, as well as the research objectives. The main practical results of the study of the connection of a real solar power plant to the distribution network using the co-simulation tool are presented. Analysis of their adequacy indicates that the discussed approach of modelling for the study of transient modes of operation of distribution networks in power systems is very promising.

articleTitle: Co-simulation of behavioral and technical decisions: an application to impact analysis of EV charging on hosting capacity of LV distribution network
abstract: The energy transition brings an increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) aligning Swiss Energy Strategy 2050. It is important for the grid planner to anticipate the possible impact of EV charging on the hosting capacity (HC) of electricity distribution network in the next years. To identify and quantify such impact, the evolution model of EV fleets, the electrical network topology and the access to proprietary data are equivalently necessary. This work studies a low voltage distribution network (LVDN) for a touristic area located in Swiss Alpine region in collaboration with the local distribution system operators (DSOs). We approach this issue with an innovative method that combines inspired agent-based model implementing insights from a Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH) and an engineering model of the local distribution grid. The co-simulation results indicate that the power demand from EVs charging will have a significant impact on the LVDN’s hosting capacity, especially on holidays’ eves. The DSOs should advance proactive measures to prepare for future scenarios. The developed co-simulation model can be used to explore and evaluate potential solutions for network planning and design.

articleTitle: Cost-benefit analysis of new levers to decrease high voltage constraints created by distributed generation
abstract: This paper presents an analytical method to compare the technical and economic performance of different levers to decrease high voltage constraints and thus maximise the hosting capacity of existing distribution networks. Based on several yearly load and generation power profiles at a 10-minute time-step, this analysis involves the calculation of various key indicators to evaluate not only the ability of any lever to eliminate voltage limits violations but also its influence in the power losses and the net present cost for the community. This study focuses on medium-voltage feeders hosting loads and generators.

articleTitle: Advancing the energy transition: a participative system engineering process for digital solutions in renewable energy communities
abstract: The novel regulatory framework on Energy Communities (ECs) is a first step towards a decentralized energy supply. In a next step, the regulatory framework could be used to ensure certain power limits within the EC enabling higher hosting capacities in the electric grid. However, ECs require digital solutions for fitting within the local limits of the distribution grid while handling complex tasks such as controlling flexible loads or performing invoicing processes. These needs require suitable system engineering processes specifically developed for ECs. Therefore, the paper proposes a system engineering process that was established during the implementation of a real-world solution in an Austrian village. The result shows a structured process combining well-established tools, such as the Double Diamond process and the IEC 62559 use case methodology.

articleTitle: Bidirectional EV smart charging in buildings with public parking (V2B): UC representation using the e-mobility systems architecture framework
abstract: The rapid growth of e-mobility is making control of peak demand in the power system increasingly challenging. Bidirectional EV charging, and in particular vehicle-to-building (V2B) strategies can support buildings and grid with necessary flexibility and load balancing, while helping offset load intermittency from renewable energy generation. This paper depicts a V2B use case (UC) on long-term smart charging for energy management of large public facilities. The analysis is supported with details from a V2B implementation at Porto Airport, in Portugal, where this UC is being tested as part of the EU-funded DriVe2X project. The UC is comprehensively explained with visual support from interoperable layer representations from the E-Mobility Systems Architecture (EMSA) framework. Modelling of e-mobility UCs with the EMSA helps demonstrate its market and technical requirements, as well as the ensuing benefits for the relevant actors, thus facilitating understanding and implementation of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) strategies and technologies.

articleTitle: Operation analysis of modified Sen transformer for flexible distribution interconnection
abstract: Flexible distribution network is an effective solution to improve the operation performance of distribution system, and soft open point (SOP) is regarded as the key equipment of flexible distribution network. However, the installation and operation cost of SOP based on fully controlled power electronic devices are relatively high, which limits the practical application of SOP in distribution networks. To solve this problem, a novel flexible interconnection device based on modified Sen transformer (MST) is considered. The power control mechanism of MST is illustrated, and the node voltage conditions that limit MST access are derived. Then, the node power regulation capability of MST is described in detail, and the impact of system operating states on the operational boundary of MST is analysed. A 10.5kV distribution network in Tianjin is used to verify the regulation perfor- mance of MST. Results indicate that MST can independently regulate the active and reactive power of the controlled bus to the desired level.

articleTitle: Analyzing impact of capacitive reactive power flows at T-D interfaces
abstract: Increased flow of capacitive reactive power (CRP) from distribution grid to transmission grid is a cause of concern for system operators. One of such concerns is how this CRP flow affects the voltage and line losses of the system. Furthermore, reactive power flow at the T-D interfaces is limited by gid codes. In this paper the analysis is done for a MV network in DIgSILENT Power Factory to show how changing load characteristics impact the system parameters and flow of reactive power at T-D interfaces.

articleTitle: Accurate federated learning with uncertainty quantification for distributed energy resource forecasting applied to smart grids planning and operation: the ALAMO vision
abstract: This paper presents the ALAMO vision, which is a research project that aims at developing technologies to facilitate the planning and operation of power grids with very high penetration of Distributed Energy Resources, while at the same time assuring the privacy of the main actors on the demand side. The ALAMO project will address outstanding research challenges related to the development of accurate forecasting algorithms based on Federated Learning (e.g., forecasting in-front and behind-the-meter PV production); as well as challenges related to producing sharped and well-calibrated quantifications of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty for such forecasting models. Finally, use-cases will be carefully crafted to understand how FL forecasts and uncertainty estimates can be incorporated into operational planning and operation tools. The use-cases will be demonstrated in virtual and physical testbeds in Portugal, USA, and Brazil.

articleTitle: Effects of exceptional high electricity market price driven electricity consumption flexibility on customers’ peak powers and power-based tariffs
abstract: Distribution system operators (DSOs) are facing significant changes happening in the customer loads. DSOs can develop their pricing to incentivise customers to use network capacity more efficiently. Peak power-based tariffs have been one alternative that some DSOs have already implemented also for their small-scale customers. In the Finnish case, the Energy Authority (regulator) has given a recommendation for harmonised tariff structure if power-based tariffs are introduced by DSOs. In previous studies it has been also shown that customers’ monthly peak powers are more stable basis of DSO’s charges than traditional energy-based charges. In this paper we study how volatile the basis of distribution bills would power-based tariffs have been during the exceptional energy year 2022, when electricity market spot prices in Finland increased significantly and customers were more flexible. The study is made using hourly electricity consumption data of 1610 customers during 1.1.2019–31.11.2023. We found that the monthly peak powers of customers are more stable basis for distribution fees during the exceptional year of the electricity market than energy consumption, but the recommended harmonised power-based fee appears to be even more volatile basis of charges from DSO’s cost recovery perspective.

articleTitle: Assessing LV networks hosting capacity for increasing PV penetration via Monte-Carlo simulations
abstract: Due to the rapid increase in residential PV capacity, it gets more and more difficult for an LV grid to absorb power at peak hours due to overvoltage issues, causing concerns to DSOs and prosumers who are temporarily unable to inject power into the grid. Monte-Carlo simulations were performed with a parametrized LV feeder model and with input parameters representing typical feeder characteristics in Belgium, in order to gain insights on the risk factors for PV-related overvoltages. The simulations’ outputs highlighted the influence of the different feeder characteristics and among the influential parameters, the feeder cable type presents the largest impact, with a notable influence of the neutral conductor impedance. The overall risk for overvoltage occurrences obtained in the simulations was relatively aligned with the number of complaints actually received by the DSO, confirming on a high-level basis the validity of the modelling approach and the statistical exercise. Without counteracting measures, the risk of prosumers enduring overvoltages is expected to increase fourfold in the future, based on projected PV penetration levels in households. Similar Monte-Carlo approaches can be used to assess the effectiveness of different possible mitigation measures, although it is important to keep in mind that the quality of the statistical outputs is largely dependent on the quality of the input parameters used for the simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal connection nodes conceptualization for battery energy storage systems
abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual model for optimizing the location of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) within a power grid. Connection nodes are critical as their placement significantly impacts overall system performance and efficiency. Existing research utilizes various techniques like convex optimization, analytical methods, and AI-based algorithms to address this issue. Optimal BESS sizing and location planning is crucial for maximizing renewable energy integration and maintaining grid stability. A study demonstrates this by proposing a robust optimization model for allocating energy storage in a distributed grid with multiple renewable sources. This paper presents a conceptual model based on a multi-node test system. It focuses on key BESS functions (services) within a distributed power supply network. The model aims to identify the optimal location, capacity, and charging/discharging strategy for the energy storage system within a specific, yet non-unique, grid topology. This emphasizes the practical application of optimal BESS placement in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, the model considers the technological characteristics of BESS units. This includes nominal power and energy capacity, alongside location attributes, and cycle efficiency parameters for effective service provision. Integrating these factors is essential for optimal BESS allocation.

articleTitle: Adaptive network partitioning and aggregation in response to operational variabilities in distribution network
abstract: Utilising photovoltaic (PV) inverters for reactive power compensation (RPC) presents an innovative method for voltage regulation. As the proportion of distributed PV increases, distributed control technology has become instrumental in enhancing the flexibility and reliability of the distribution network (DN), ensuring its safe and efficient operation. It necessitates the segmentation of DN into distinct clusters, establishing subordination between PVs and regional controllers for efficacious distributed control. However, conventional methods may overlook the changing scenarios of DN operating status caused by PV and load power fluctuations. In addition, the time-varying partitioning results will cause frequent changes in the subordination between PV and cluster, increasing the partition computation and the difficulty for PV regulation. To mitigate these challenges, this paper first proposes a partitioning strategy employing the Coupling Coefficient Index (CCI), grouping PVs and corresponding nodes sensitive to reactive power. Secondly, the aggregation method for partitioning results in different time segment is given to simplify the partitioning calculation. The proposed method can accommodate diverse operational scenarios caused by PV and load power fluctuations. Finally, the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed method are corroborated within the IEEE 123 node test system. The proposed method will enhance the voltage regulation capabilities of PVs, thereby increasing the DN’s hosting capacity for PV.

articleTitle: Application of artificial intelligence for the thermal rating of a high voltage cable system
abstract: This paper briefly summarises the investigations carried out by Wiener Netze on the application of artificial intelligence for the thermal rating of high voltage cables in urban areas. As part of this project, various stationary and dynamic load tests were carried out on a 400 kV cable installation over a period of three years. In this time more than 70 million data points of various parameters such as currents, temperatures, soil moistures and climatic quantities were recorded. Based on this data, the thermal dynamics of the cable system were analysed using descriptive statistics. Established calculation methods were verified and, among other things, machine learning models were also trained and validated. It could be shown that machine learning models can recognise and depict complex processes that influence the thermal behaviour of the cable system using data alone. Furthermore, data-driven models were created that can not only map the cable temperature but can also be used for cable temperature forecasts for different time horizons within intraday forecasting with over 99 % accuracy. The lack of robustness of the black box models could be countered by appropriate validation methods for the cable arrangement under investigation.

articleTitle: Short-term scheduled power reserve: an artificial neural network approach
abstract: Renewable energy sources like photovoltaic systems (PV) often result in significant active power imbalances due to their variable nature. Despite their predictability, the uncertainty in their power production increases the complexity of planned power generation and necessitates the activation of costly and polluting power reserves commonly provided by conventional generators. This paper proposes an intelligent control technique to predict and replace diesel-based power reserves by faster, more economical and environmentally friendly reserves provided by a battery energy storage system (BESS). Following a power imbalance, a frequency droop controller ensures the primary reserve support from a BESS within a few seconds. Building upon the assumption that the variations of PV power are persistent within a 10-minute window, a secondary reserve for the next 5 minutes is commanded from an artificial neural network (ANN)-based adaptive module. This module predicts battery power references with a 1-minute time increment based on the PV and diesel generator power measured 5 minutes earlier. The proposed method's efficacy is showcased through its application on an islanded AC microgrid. Real-time simulations are performed using the Opal-RT simulator, revealing enhanced power balancing along with reductions in both operating costs and CO2 emissions.

articleTitle: Typical protection configuration with self-healing functionality for a super-large urban distribution network
abstract: A resilient and intelligent distribution network is an essential component of the construction of a new power system. In recent years, Shanghai, as an international mega-city, has undertaken comprehensive development in the planning and construction of its distribution network. The city has focused on establishing an interconnected distribution network, achieving dual-source power supply, and dual-loop network connections. Additionally, the self-healing control system achieves millisecond-level rapid fault isolation and automatic power restoration through relay protection, thereby realizing the self-healing of the distribution network, improving power supply reliability and enhancing hosting capacity. In response to this resilient and intelligent dual-source, dual-loop distribution network framework, this paper provides a typical relay protection configuration scheme. The proposed scheme has been practically applied in the distribution network in Shanghai, demonstrating significant engineering practicality.

articleTitle: Windows to reduced leakage and interference without any influence on harmonic components of phasor and power flow measurements
abstract: The changes in the electricity grid pose new challenges for the measurement of power flows in the grid. The non-linear behavior on both the generation and load side can lead to the simultaneous observation of reversed power flows on different harmonics on one line. In order to gain a comprehensive understanding of the power flows, it is necessary to measure the harmonic components separately. This requires the measurement of voltage and current with usable phase information, such as in harmonic phase measurement. In conjunction with a fluctuating fundamental frequency, leakages occur in existing technologies, which devalue the phase information of the harmonics. In order to eliminate the symptoms of this problem, increasingly complex methods are used or the phase information is often omitted altogether. With the increasing use of power electronics, interharmonic disturbances are also increasing. At the same time, fast control loops lead to an increase in volatility, whereby the usual duration of steady-state behavior decreases, which makes it necessary to reduce the averaging times for measurements. This work focuses on the measurement of harmonic signal components as they are usually performed for synchrophasors, harmonic phases or power quality measurements in electrical power systems. A class of windows is defined which, in combination with a periodic superposition of the signals, has no influence on the measurement of harmonic components. The combination of special windows and superposition shown here is invisible for harmonic signal components, but can significantly reduce the measurement errors caused by incorrect estimation of the fundamental frequency and inter-harmonic signal components. The commonly used rectangular window is a member of this class and is used as a reference for the evaluation. However, Bartlett, Hann and sine ramp base windows can also be designed as members of this class. All windows have a length of 2 timing intervals and are executed with 50% overlap. It is shown that an implementation of these windows is possible without significant additional effort. Leakage is caused by a difference between the fundamental frequency of the analyzed signal, which often varies over time, and the fundamental frequency assumed by the measurement system. The simulation results for a frequency offset of 100 mHz show time-variant measurement results of the measurand of fundamental wave when using a rectangular window. Other windows show a much better behavior and a higher stability. Of course, the phase error must still be compensated for separately. Interharmonic interference can cause the interference to spread over a wide range of measured harmonics. The rectangular window has a wide spread with limited attenuation. The best results with the lowest interference are obtained for the sine ramp base window. The sine ramp base window in combination with the superposition with a measurement interval of one line cycle seems to be the best choice for the measurement of harmonic components, whereby the reduced measurement interval reduces the risk of erroneous measurements due to transient behavior within the measurement period.

articleTitle: Behaviour of grid-oriented controlled heat pumps
abstract: The German government plans to install 500 000 heat pumps a year starting in 2024, which, among other things, will lead to an additional electrical load on the distribution grid. The revised Energy Industry Act § 14a enables the grid-oriented use of flexibilities such as heat pumps in Germany. To estimate the effects of grid-oriented control during the blocking phase and re-enabling and to be able to take them into account in models or grid calculations, it is essential to know the behaviour. Manufacturers surveyed were currently unable to make any statements about the behaviour of their heat pump in the various operating phases during external blocking. This paper shows examples of an inverter and a fixed-speed heat pump to estimate the behaviour of heat pumps in the event of an external disconnection by the distribution grid operator. It is shown that the behaviour differs depending on the type of heat pump and the operating phase before the blocking period.

articleTitle: Roseau Load Flow: a modern software package for the modelling and steady-state simulation of power distribution grids
abstract: The concept of modelling and simulation of electricity grids, in particular for power flow and short-circuit analysis, has been around for decades. Numerous numerical methods and software tools thus have already been developed for that purpose. Nonetheless, it is still the subject of active research, driven by new needs of power grid operators and by advances in the fields of applied mathematics and software engineering. This paper introduces the result of such recent research, namely:Roseau Load Flow, a new tool for power distribution grid simulation that is especially suitable for the analysis of low- and medium-voltage grids. We describe its specific features and main design choices, highlighting howRoseau Load Flowdifferentiates from existing solvers and improves over the state-of-the-art in the area of modelling and simulation of power distribution grids. Then, we demonstrate its capabilities by evaluating the hosting capacity of a real low-voltage grid for distributed generators equipped with Volt-VAr and Volt-Watt regulations.

articleTitle: The value of AC optimal power flow models in the assessment of distribution grid electric vehicle and photovoltaic power plant hosting capacity – case study in Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) share is continuing its rapid growth. The share in total sales has more than tripled from the year 20 20 (4%) to 2022 (14%). Production from photovoltaic (PV) power plants in the year 2022 increased by 270 TWh, representing a 26% rise, reaching nearly 1300 TWh with the largest growth of all renewable technologies for the first time in history. In this paper, we assess the potential of installed power of EV charging stations (EV CS) and PV plants in real-world distribution grids. Hosting capacity (HC) calculation for both EV CS and PV plants is solved using two different approaches, one by using the AC Optimal Power Flow (AC OPF) formulation modelled in the Python programming language and the other solved iteratively with power flow simulation in DIgSILENT PowerFactory (DPF). To assess the benefits of the two approaches, we compare the solutions in terms of complexity and accuracy. AC OPF showed 3.3% higher results for EV HC and 21.6% higher for PV HC. Furthermore, the results detected weak points in the grid that can be used by the Distribution System Operator to identify transformers or lines that require replacement, to allow further electrification in the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Enhancing the reliability and power quality in Burundian power distribution network: sharing an experience
abstract: Burundi (Africa) is having dense population and lesser T&D network. The installed generation capacity as on Sept 2023, is 106.1MW.The total length of T&D line is 511.7 ckt km. REGIDESO ((Régie de Distribution d’Eau et d’Electricité du BURUNDI) is government owned and major power distribution company in Burundi. At some of the places in the existing distribution system, issues of Quality of Power have been raised by customers. To enhance the reliability and quality of power network is being studied through various software so as to be prepared for the upcoming load growth and upliftment of living standard of people. The present paper consists of study case taken for one of the 6.6kV feeders emanating from RN1 110/30/6.6kV substation. Recommendations are made to improve the performance of the existing distribution power system. Some of the suggestions are conventional mitigation practices like harmonic mitigation, power factor improvement. Use of emerging technological solutions are also suggested to increase the power hosting capacity.

articleTitle: Concept of a device for universal manipulation of charging processes of electric vehicles to increase distribution system hosting capacity
abstract: The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energies is making the energy supply system increasingly dynamic. This dynamic, together with increasing electrification in the mobility sector, leads to the question of how hosting capacity in the electricity distribution grid can be increased. This publication shows a possibility to increase the hosting capacity by a universal, intelligent control of charging processes of electric vehicles in the (private) AC area. The special feature of the controller is its integration into a standard charging cable, which has the following advantages: Portability and thus targeted and possible short-term usage. The avoidance of stranded investments in case of grid expansion. Maximum compatibility thanks to uniform standardization and the possibility of retrofitting existing charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Applicaiton of protection strategy base on the rate of current change in AC/DC distribution network
abstract: In order to solve the problem of insufficient operation reliability and protection-selected ability of Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) converter in Alternating Current (AC)/Direct Current (DC) power distribution system under the short circuit between DC electrodes, this paper studies the protection strategy under the fault of AC/DC power distribution system, and introduces the relay protection strategy based on the rate of current change, which improves the sensitivity of fault characteristics and the accuracy of protection action under the reaction fault state. In this paper, a simulation test based on PSCAD/EMTDC platform is carried out based on the application case of the inter-electrode short-circuit fault in the four-terminal loop AC/DC hybrid distribution system. The simulation results verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the action behavior of the protection policy under the faults within and out of the system, and provide an effective theoretical basis and technical support for improving the operational reliability of AC/DC hybrid power distribution system.

articleTitle: A visualisation tool for electrical installation sizing of car parks in collective housing
abstract: Enedis, the French main Distribution System Operator (DSO), started a series of studies to anticipate the massive increase in electric car use. A critical aspect is the sizing of car parks in collective housing due to the increasing number of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE). In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach to monitor on actual consumption data key quantities used for electrical installation sizing: the reference power of an EVSE and the coincidence factor.

articleTitle: Network planning strategies to enable 100% renewable energy
abstract: In many parts of the world, the push towards a renewable energy future causes voltage range exceedances and thermal capacity violations. Significant concerns arise over the future extent of these violations as business-as-usual mitigation methods threaten to saddle the electricity industry with significant costs. This unacceptable outcome cannot be countered using the existing design philosophy and impels us to think differently to achieve an acceptable and cost-effective outcome. This paper introduces a new paradigm for the design and planning of distribution networks to enable them to support a fully renewable energy system. The world-wide movement towards a fossil-fuel-free energy system compels us to consider significant increases in both load and generation within the distribution system. This obviously impacts the available voltage range and the thermal capacity of the existing networks. Dynamic methods for managing voltages and power flows must replace old design practices to enable networks to host both the growing distributed generation, and the growing load of a renewable future. Effective voltage management, voltage balancing, and harmonic mitigation is realisable with the modern power electronic systems described in in this paper. In addition, strategies are also presented to address the impact of both growing renewable generation and increasing load.

articleTitle: Electric vehicle charging energy management for voltage control in low-voltage distribution networks
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) serve as valuable flexible loads for demand response (DR) programs. These types of programs aim to adapt the consumption or production of a load using external signals to match specific grid requirements. For instance, ancillary system services can use EVs to assist in grid operation by adjusting their charging profile to match with the operational conditions of the power grid. This paper presents an EV charging energy management system (EVC-EMS), designed to extract EV-based flexibility at local charging stations, manage EV charging rates to compute and inform an external flexibility service provider (FSP) of available demand flexibility, and dispatch flexibility upon request. As a proof-of-concept for the functionality of the EVC-EMS, a test scenario focusing on exploiting EV charging station flexibility to manage voltage in a low-voltage (LV) distribution network has been developed. The results show that coordinating the EV supply equipment with the help of the EVC- EMS can be successfully utilized for a fast DR program. The tested DR scheme can perform voltage control in the LV network by considerably reducing overvoltages.

articleTitle: Participation of PV installations connected to LV grids in voltage support for the MV network
abstract: The Flex#Cantal project aimed to demonstrate how PV power plants connected to the Low Voltage (LV) grid can contribute to voltage support on the Medium Voltage (MV) grid. Led by Enedis, the main French DSO, in collaboration with Hespul and AURA-EE, this project focused on activating reactive power regulation of PV power plants with a total installed capacity of 8MW, connected to the LV distribution grid (400V), to address voltage issues on the MV grid (20 kV) and increase hosting capacity. The French demonstration described in this paper focused on activating a constant power factor (0.944 lagging) of the PV plants connected to LV grid and related to MV grid through public LV/MV transformers. Three out of five different MV feeders, experiencing reverse power flows and consequent voltage rise, were selected to conduct the experimentation.

articleTitle: Unlocking network hosting capacity for flexible queue management
abstract: The UK's path to net zero emissions relies on integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) into the power network. However, this creates increased loading at certain points. Traditional methods for evaluating connection requests, based on rated capacity, have led to significant queues awaiting connections date while network reinforcement work is completed. Yet, RES often don't operate at full capacity due to resource availability or market conditions. This can lead to untapped network capacity at some times of day or year. In addition, diversity in the generation profiles among renewable energy sources or flexibility in customer demands was not traditionally taken into consideration when assessing capacity headroom. The Diversified Flexible Queue Management (DFQM) project aims to leverage data intelligence to manage the connection queue more efficiently, assessing customer loads and generation flexibility in real-time to speed up connections. In this paper, two novel approaches aimed at improving hosting capacity within distribution networks, particularly at Grid Supply Points (GSPs), are presented. The performance of the two approaches have been compared and analysed through GSPs within Northern Powergrid’s licensed area and an assessment of the potential increase in available capacity is presented.

articleTitle: EMINENT, a method for assessing interoperability maturity
abstract: The energy transition involves accelerated renewable energy integration and the electrification of energy systems. Many of these changes have dramatic impacts on the distribution planning and operation system infrastructure. A diverse and interconnected energy system is more flexible and resilient to changes and disruptions. Interoperability enables different components of the energy system to communicate and coordinate effectively. There is a need for interoperability with increasing diversity of energy sources, as we shift from traditional, centralized fossil-fuel based systems to a more decentralized and diverse set of energy sources. This paper describes the development of EMINENT, an Interoperability Maturity Model (IMM) created by int:net, the actors involved, the goals of the model and how it can be used to track progress across the entire energy interoperability community. The constant evolution and improvements within the sector's environment contribute to a cyclical nature, shaping the maturity of systems over time. Rather than a straightforward progression, the level of maturity serves as a dynamic snapshot, encapsulating a specific period in the ever-changing landscape of the energy sector. Applying the IMM will allow various communities to evaluate their current levels of interoperability. It will involve organizational alignment, while highlighting the various community strengths and in turn reflect the current state of the energy sector.

articleTitle: PARMENIDES – ideal voltage sensory placement for battery storage operation optimization
abstract: To optimize the operation of a low-voltage distribution grid, battery storage systems can be efficiently managed at an optimal point by using a grid capacity management system. However, this requires more detailed information about the state of a grid than is usually available. This gap can be bridged by installing additional sensors, and the number of sensors can be minimized through innovative state estimation approaches. The presented approach allows the training of Machine Learning (ML) models capable of predicting the grid state when provided with operational data obtained through load flow calculations from the same grid. The models are trained to predict unknown voltage values based on assumed known data. The conducted experiments aimed at identifying the optimal locations for these voltage measurements to determine the ideal placement for sensory equipment in the grid and assess the estimation error. The results revealed that for both grids specific sensor placement can be identified where models perform very well with a low error and demonstrate a high level of prediction accuracy. Moreover, statements about the ideal placement of the sensors were derived from experiments.

articleTitle: PARMENIDES – enabling flexibility provision in renewable energy communities through an ontology-driven interoperable ICT architecture
abstract: PARMENIDES addresses challenges in the energy system by providing interoperable solutions that harness the potential of Hybrid Energy Storage Systems. A key innovation is the PARMENIDES Energy Community Ontology streamlining energy community operations through optimized energy flows and local energy maximization. The project introduces an Energy Management System for Hybrid Energy Storage Systems, utilizing ontology as a knowledge base and for extended information inference. Diverse PARMENIDES use cases cover scenarios ranging from passive energy community participation to fully automated optimization. These use cases vary in automation levels, optimization features, and flexibility strategies. The developed Information and Communication Technology architecture ensures interoperability, reliability, and security. Components include a Grid Capacity System, Grid Monitoring Devices and Smart Meters, an Information and Configuration System as a central repository for knowledge and data and an Energy Management System. Specific instantiations of the architecture will be implemented in the Austrian and Swedish pilots.

articleTitle: Bidirectional electric vehicle smart charging in public charging stations (V2G): use case representation using the e-mobility systems architecture framework
abstract: The global shift towards electric vehicles is expected to result in more than 1 billion electric vehicles (EVs) by 2050, providing a substantial source of flexibility for the power system and enhancing the integration of renewable energy resources. The DriVe2X project aims to create new expertise, information and communication technology (ICT) solutions, and hardware technologies to handle the mass deployment of electric vehicles in Europe. Explores diverse scenarios of bidirectional electric vehicle smart charging, including vehicle-to-grid, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-building interactions. The paper focusses on vehicle-to-grid strategies, specifically a demonstration in Terni, Italy. The paper presents vehicle-to-grid use case that enable business cases harnessing the full potential of the bidirectional charging strategies. It describes the complex coordination between stakeholders in public charging stations, creating an ecosystem that connects electric vehicles to the energy grid, improving grid stability. The Terni vehicle-to-grid business model relies on strategic interactions among stakeholders to manage the integration of EVs with the energy grid. The distribution system operator ensures grid stability and allows the bidirectional flow of electricity, making electric vehicle drivers an integrated part of the energy system and electricity market.

articleTitle: Inclusion of dynamic management of flexible electric vehicles in the network planning stage to increase hosting capacity
abstract: In this paper, we will present a planning methodology that considers the possibility of running an operation in which flexible assets are managed by coupling the planning stage with the network operation stage. The case study presented will focus on the determination of low voltage grid capacity by proposing a system that determines whether it is adequate or needs to be reinforced in a framework of massive deployment of electric vehicles (EVs). A novel planning methodology is proposed, integrating flexible asset management into network operation to determine grid capacity in the presence of EVs. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of controlled charging in alleviating transformer overloading and increasing hosting capacity. This research contributes insights for distribution system operators and policymakers in adapting to the evolving energy landscape.

articleTitle: Road towards a stress test: stressing the digital twin with current measurements and future loads
abstract: This paper presents a methodology used by ewz, to conduct a stress test in the low-voltage grid with the aim to proactively analyse the potential effects of the evolving energy strategy. In short, the objective is to find future weaknesses in our grid by using our digital twin and increasing dimensions like penetration of e-mobility and PV according to our forecasts to find the weakest components in the grid. Within this test a year-by-year analysis of the low voltage grid is performed, bridging the gap between today's loads in the grid to the expected future loads by 2050. This approach allows for the evaluation of future load effects on the low-voltage grid, enabling analysis of potential shortcomings and their temporal occurrence.

articleTitle: Whole system thinking: reducing curtailment of renewables and increasing societal value via targeted network reinforcement
abstract: Amidst a backdrop of increasing prevalence of Distributed Generation and growing curtailment of renewable energy, the hypothesis posed within this report seeks to understand if there is financial and environmental value on the whole energy system through increasing distribution network capacity. The modelling concluded that the potential cost and carbon benefits of reducing distribution network curtailment ranges from £324 million and £116 million to £17 billion and £753 million to cost and carbon respectively from 2023 to 2034 based on two network modelling methodologies.

articleTitle: Grid technologies to increase the capacity of unbalanced low-voltage networks: a model-based approach to unlock flexible resources management and increase PV penetration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel network technology designed to address two paramount objectives for the Distribution System Operator. First, it proposes a comprehensive methodology that calculates the needed flexibility and orchestrates the operation of flexible resources within the network by adhering to technically and economically optimal strategies. Second, it presents a sophisticated tool for intelligently planning new photovoltaic connections in the network while identifying vulnerable areas that warrant network reinforcement. In pursuit of the first objective, this technology offers an accurate representation of Low Voltage network behaviour. Critically, it exhibits computational efficiency, ensuring real-time flexibility management and activation of operation strategies that are both technically and economically optimal. Concerning the second objective of intelligent planning, Distribution System Operators increasingly seek tools that empower them to generate maps depicting the nodal capacity growth potential for new connections within their networks. This involves precise insights into the Hosting Capacity of these connections, as well as supportive systems aiding in the strategic placement of new connections catering to generation, consumption, or a combination of both. The outcomes presented in this paper are derived from a meticulous analysis of real network topology data and meter readings obtained from a distribution network in southern Spain.

articleTitle: Optimal storage integration in a low-voltage grid to maximise its hosting capacity on distributed generation
abstract: The increased distributed generation share on the grids is challenging their operation. Storage technologies are considered the most essential alternative for overcoming these challenges and enlarging the hosting capacity of low-voltage grids on distributed generation (rooftop photovoltaics). This work develops a model that examines the integration of storage systems from a technical, economic and ecological perspective. Four scenarios are developed, calculated and evaluated, with two scenarios dealing with customer-installed battery storage systems with different operating modes, one based on a grid-installed central battery storage system, and one using a hydrogen storage system.

articleTitle: Accelerating energy transition in Portugal
abstract: Energy Transition has been accelerating and is a clear commitment for E-REDES, the main Portuguese Distribution System Operator (DSO) In Portugal's mainland, between 2022 and 2025, the installed power of renewable power plants connected to the distribution network will increase by approximately 80% and double by 2030. The number of individual self-consumption systems connected to the distribution network has also been accelerating, and between 2022 and 2023, more self-consumption systems were installed than in the 2015 -2021 period. Furthermore, Energy Communities are emerging and are expected to grow significantly (at the present moment there are 49 in operation). At last, Electric mobility charging infrastructure has increased substantially since 2019, and the new infrastructure has doubled during the past two years. To respond to and facilitate this transition, E-REDES has been implementing a set of initiatives in three strategic pillars: new organisation, proactive information, and digitisation & automation:<list list-type="bullet" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <list-item> In 2022, the Sprint Verde (SV) Project introduced a new Agile methodology, starting to set daily meetings with all parties and establishing a single point of contact for customers. </list-item> <list-item> New tools were created to provide proactive and valuable information to customers. As well as dashboards where customers can find information about their processes, valuable information about power availability in the network was shared on our website. </list-item> <list-item> Digital functionalities such as web services were implemented to automate processes, Follow your Request app and a Digital Counter. </list-item> </list> To sum up, this paper will describe the strategy developed by E-REDES, together with customers, to face the challenges of the present and the future, to accelerate the energy transition.

articleTitle: Investigation of the user behaviour of EV drivers and consequent grid impacts
abstract: This paper presents the methodology adopted within the EU-project "XL-Connect" for investigating the future Electric Vehicle (EV) user behaviour and consequent impacts for the energy system. The user behaviour has been investigated through literature research, a survey and expert interviews. The findings from the user behaviour analysis have been used to formulate the "XL-Connect" framework evaluating grid impacts of EVs. A probabilistic calculation component stands for the cornerstone of the framework, which calculates probabilistic power network state and grid security indicators based on two categories of inputs resulting from data-driven models. At first, a "Grid generator" defines grid operational or planning scenarios, which embrace grid structure properties, including network topology, electrical properties of network elements or settings of controllable assets. Secondly, a "Scenario generator" composes power injection profiles and operational uncertainty (i.e. confidence bounds) related to consumption, production, energy storage or EV (dis)charging patterns. Third, an "EV pattern generator" provides (dis)charging power profiles and spatiotemporal probability of their occurrence in a power system. The scenario parametrisation of data-driven models is based on real-world datasets and data science approaches (e.g. cluster analysis).

articleTitle: Energy optimization of an industrial cluster: a cooperative coalition approach
abstract: Large electricity consumers, such as industrial factories, are significantly affected by intermittent renewable energies and volatile electricity prices. In addition, they have limited options for immediate load shifting, as the production process is optimized favouring internal constraints over external market conditions. The creation of an energy cluster between industrial factories can provide benefits in coordinating the electricity consumption schedules, leveraging shared energy assets, reducing costs and CO2 emissions. It also providing relief to grid operators in the form of increased demand side flexibility, which can improve hosting capacity of renewable energies by adding load side control capabilities. This defines the boundaries for the creation of a cooperative coalition, where individual benefits are secondary to the global benefit of the cluster. This work presents a case study of a MILP optimization model to minimize the total costs of energy provision of an industrial cluster comprised by 6 factories, using synthetic data simulating real use cases. This framework is developed as part of the services of the Horizon Europe project “FLEX4FACT – Industrial flexibility platform for sustainable factories”.

articleTitle: A business model or a tariffing issue? Peak shaving in local distribution grids through electric vehicle fleets
abstract: This paper addresses the question how shared electric vehicle fleets, i.e. car-sharing or company fleets, can offer flexibility services for the electricity grid through smart and bidirectional charging. Specifically, the focus is on the perspective of DSOs, analysing the peak shaving potential at a common grid node. The paper provides initial insights from one of the case studies of the research project GAMES and demonstrates the economic potential under current and also possible future market designs for a station-based car sharing scheme in Zurich, Switzerland. The model deployed in this work is a linear economic dispatch model, providing optimal charging and discharging schedules for the electric vehicles of the fleet. The results suggest, that technically there could be the potential to reduce the annual peak load of the Zurich grid area by up to 4%. However, significant changes in the tariffing structure for charging peak loads need to be implemented to make business models for such use cases economically feasible.

articleTitle: Wide-area distribution assessment to increase hosting capacity in an energy transition landscape
abstract: Today's distribution planners must prepare the distribution grid for the impact of new energy resources and electrified loads. This paper presents a framework for addressing these impacts by combining hosting capacity analysis with load/generation forecasts to identify grid-wide mitigation solutions. This framework aids distribution planning engineers in making informed decisions for near and long-term planning, prioritize mitigation strategies, and optimize the path towards the desired distribution system state. The efficiency of the framework supports planning efforts in meeting decarbonization and electrification targets in the utilities energy transition landscape.

articleTitle: A novel container-based approach for integrating solar forecast in real-time simulation and model predictive control
abstract: This paper presents an interdisciplinary, novel approach for incorporating day-ahead solar forecast obtained using numeric models into a real-time simulation framework for low-voltage microgrid analysis. The solar forecast data were integrated into the grid simulation at the information, communication, and function levels, utilising the data model and communication structure defined in the international standard IEC 61850. Given the forecast of solar power and a reference trajectory defined by the upper-level grid management system over a sliding predictive time window, a model predictive control scheme has been implemented to compute control setpoints for solar curtailment in a simplified simulation scenario, regardless of the power flow over lines. In the virtualised environment with decentralised intelligent controllers in containers, the control setpoints are communicated between the IEC 61850 client and server and implemented as measures for solar peak-shaving. The test results showed that the model predictive control scheme outperformed trivial linear control methods, suggesting that the container-based virtualisation concept has the potential to be further exploited for practical use cases at the utility and energy market level, and the IEC 61850 standard could be a feasible solution in terms of grid communication and forecast integration.

articleTitle: Implementation of a hybrid grid tariff in Norway: distributional effects, metered consumer response and design trade-offs
abstract: The development of distributed energy resources calls for shift in grid tariff design. Most DSOs in Norway implemented a hybrid grid tariff with both a capacity and a time-of-use energy term. In this paper, we have investigated the redistributional effects to determine whether any consumer groups experience disproportionate changes in costs. In addition, metered data was analysed and compared to demand before the introduction of the grid tariff to see if consumers had responded to the grid tariff price signal. Finally, the grid tariff’s trade-offs between different grid tariff design principles were evaluated. We conclude that the grid tariff has resulted in lower costs for low-income consumers, especially those in small apartments, and vice versa for high-income consumers living in large houses with electric vehicles. The capacity intervals do not appear to have triggered any response from consumers. Further developments on the grid tariff can be conducted to improve its cost reflectivity, such as by moving to continuous measured peak demand and dynamic pricing based on real-time grid status, but at the cost of simplicity and predictability, and hence acceptance. Time-of-use energy terms has negative impacts in the long-term due to synchronised demand response resulting in increased peak loads.

articleTitle: Impact of neutral conductor sizing on LV networks hosting capacity - a Monte-Carlo analysis
abstract: Due to the rapid increase in residential PV capacity, it gets more and more difficult for an LV grid to absorb power at peak hours due to overvoltage issues, causing concerns to DSOs and prosumers who are temporarily unable to inject power into the grid. Monte-Carlo simulations were performed with a parametrized LV feeder model representing typical feeder characteristics in Belgium, in order to notably gain insights on the impact of the feeder cable type on the risk of overvoltage occurrences. The simulations’ outputs highlighted the significant impact of the cable type, with a noteworthy influence of the neutral conductor impedance. The significance of impact of the neutral impedance is directly linked to the significance of the unbalance levels of PV production. The gain in terms of voltage excursion (|V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ph-N</sub>- V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nom</sub>|) reduction can be large for a DSO switching from asymmetrical cables (with reduced neutral cross-section) to symmetrical ones. Voltage excursion reductions of 22 to 32% are typically observed, although much larger reductions have been obtained. The reduction of the risk for overvoltage occurrences ranged from 43 to 74% depending on the asymmetrical/symmetrical cable pairs considered.

articleTitle: The development of local electricity markets for flexibility services: the case of Milan congestion management
abstract: The increasing electrification of demand, which has traditionally relied on other energy vectors (e.g., heating, cooling, and fuelling of vehicles), and the progressive introduction of renewable and non-programmable generators pose serious challenges for managing distribution networks.
